text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London trimmed some losses but still ended lower after falling by some 5 per cent early in the session. Light stop-loss selling by investment funds had contributed to the sharp falls. By the close London's May was just $40 down at $1,570 a tonne, after recovering from a week's low of $1,515. Resistance is now seen at between $1,590-$1,610 while support is seen at $1,530. Traders noted sizeable rolling of May positions into July, which also lost $40 on the day closing at $1,580 a tonne.

Arabica futures in New York recovered from recent steep losses to end moderately higher, bolstered by an afternoon round of commission house buying, traders said. At the close, May stood 1.45 cents/lb firmer at 179.15 cents/lb, while second month July settled 1.40 cents/lb higher, to 164.75 cents/lb. The back months finished up 3.30 to down 1.00 cent/lb. Dealers said some of the day's buying was fueled by talk of cooler weather moving into Brazil's southern Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina states. However, forecasters said there was no chance of damaging frost. After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged at 83,078 60-kg bags as of April 3. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange added.

BRAZIL - Stevedores at the key Brazilian port of Santos will decide whether to stage further strikes after meeting representatives from the steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) on Monday, a union official said. The stevedores effectively stopped loading and unloading operations at the port for three days from April 2 in protest at a ruling allowing Cosipa workers to conduct stevedore operations at Cosipa's private terminal. A nationwide stoppage called by the National Stevedores Federation received 85 per cent support. All members returned to work as agreed on April 5 and operations at Santos were normal except at the Cosipa terminal which is still paralyzed, it was added.

UNITED STATES - US green coffee roastings for the week ended March 29 totalled approximately 270,000 60-kg bags, up from 260,000 bags the previous week and compared with 265,000 bags in the corresponding period one year-ago, Complete Coffee Coverage reports. Cumulative roastings so far totalled 4.475 mn 60-kg bags, versus 4.335 mn bags in the same year-ago period.

COLOMBIA - Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation raised the internal price per 125-kg bags of coffee by 1.99 per cent to 339,875 pesos, a spokesman said. The new price, up from 333,250 pesos, was based on average international price of $2.02 per pound of coffee in New York. The Federation has now raised the internal price of coffee seven times since January 31. It has been cut twice in the same period since the Federation introduced a new moving scale formula to calculate internal prices based on the average international price.

UNITED KINGDOM - Coffee imports in December 1996 amounted to 405,615 bags, up from last year's 200,591 bags. This brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to 3.114 mn bags, up almost 12 per cent on last year's 2.783 mn bags. Total imports in 1994 amounted to 3.395 mn bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/December 1996 were Indonesia (362,600 vs 293,000 bags), Colombia (257,100 vs 196,800 bags) and Costa Rica (235,900 vs 335,800 bags).

Coffee exports in December 1996 reached 46,473 bags, up from 34,542 bags exported in December 1995. This brought total exports in 1996 up to 542,626 bags, almost unchanged against last year's 538,399 bags. Total exports in 1994 amounted to 669,382 bags. The UK exports most of its coffee in the form of solubles with Germany (115,300 vs 112,200 bags), Ireland (71,700 vs 59,000 bags) and France (46,700 vs 44,000 bags) being the main markets.
